v.rationale: Both implementations do the same core work: a nullable customer_id with a nullOnDelete foreign key added while foreign key checks are off, composite indexes (customer_id, status, created_at) and (customer_id, created_at), an id-range backfill that matches on lower(trim()) and leaves updated_at alone, and a controller that goes through the relation with a FormRequest. Both suites pass, and both passed probes for id gaps larger than the chunk, re-runs picking up orders from the previous app version, and array-status validation. impl-2 wins on the task's focus. It splits the release into three migrations (column, then indexes, then the FK last so it reuses an existing index), every down() rolls back cleanly, and the backfill uses the query builder (subquery update with whereExists and toBase()). It also adds an id tiebreaker for stable pagination and has broader tests. impl-1 puts all the DDL in one migration, which can't be resumed if it fails partway on MySQL, and its down() is broken: it fails on SQLite (confirmed) and would leave leftover indexes on MySQL. It also writes the backfill as duplicated raw SQL.
